transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because this has gotten kind of out of hand, I guess. It’s about wasps. I know that probably sounds small, but I’ve gotten to where I plan my whole summer around avoiding them. Like, I used to help with garden jobs at church, and I’ve pretty much given that up because I just can’t stand being out there if I think there might be wasps around.

Even at home, if I hear buzzing near the back porch, I won’t go out there. I’ll make my husband unload things instead, or bring things in, because I just… I can’t make myself do it. It’s embarrassing, honestly, but it’s become such a big part of how I get through the warmer months.
What is it about wasps that scares you the most?

I think it’s the feeling that something awful is about to happen, even though I know, logically, it’s just a small insect. I mean, I can say that sitting here — a wasp is little, most people would just wave it away or swat it and go on with their day. But when one gets close to me, it doesn’t feel little. It feels like this immediate danger, like my whole body is saying, “Get away right now.”

It’s not even just seeing it from far off. If it’s anywhere near me, or I hear that buzzing and think it might be close, I get this sense like I’m about to be hurt, or like something terrible is going to happen and I won’t be able to stop it. I know that probably sounds dramatic, because I do understand it’s not a bear or a car coming at me or something, but in the moment it feels that serious to me.
Outside of wasps, do you find yourself worrying excessively about lots of other things in daily life?

I don’t think so, no… at least not in the same way. I mean, I worry about normal things, like anyone does — bills, family, whether I forgot something at the store, that kind of everyday stuff — but it doesn’t take over my day the way this does.

With the wasps, it’s like everything in me reacts before I can even think. I’ll rearrange what I’m doing, avoid going outside, ask my husband to handle things… it’s very specific. I’m not sitting around all day worrying about every possible thing that could go wrong. It’s really when it has to do with wasps, or the possibility of running into one, especially when it’s warm out. Then I get worked up. Otherwise, I wouldn’t say I’m an especially nervous person in general.
Have you ever had a wasp sting that you believe started this fear?

I honestly don’t know. I mean, I’ve thought about that, because it seems like there should be some clear story, right? Like I got stung badly as a kid and then this all started. But I can’t really point to one thing like that.

I’m sure I’ve probably been stung at some point in my life, just being outside and all, but I don’t have a specific memory where I think, yes, that’s what caused it. Nothing stands out to me as some big terrible sting or emergency or anything like that. It’s more like the fear is just… there, and it’s gotten worse or more noticeable over time, especially when I’m around them.
Do you feel that your fear of wasps is stronger than the actual danger they pose?

Yes… yes, I do. I mean, sitting here like this, I can absolutely understand that a wasp is just a little insect. I know most people would probably just swat it away, or move aside, or not think much of it unless it actually stung them. I know that in my head.

But when one gets anywhere near me, it doesn’t feel like a small thing at all. It feels like something terrible is about to happen right then, like I’m in real danger even if, realistically, I’m probably not. So yes, I’d say my fear is much stronger than the actual danger. It’s like my mind knows one thing, but my body reacts like it’s something much worse.
When there aren’t any wasps around, do unwanted thoughts about wasps keep popping into your mind anyway?

Not really… I don’t think so. I mean, I might think about them if something reminds me — like if it’s warm out, or I’m planning to sit outside, or I hear buzzing and I wonder what it is. Then my mind goes there pretty quickly.

But if I’m just in the house doing normal things and there’s no reason to think about wasps, I wouldn’t say thoughts about them keep intruding on me out of nowhere. It’s more connected to the situation, I guess. Like if I know I might be around them, then I start thinking ahead about it. But they’re not just popping into my head all day for no reason.
When a wasp gets close to you, do you ever have a panic attack?

I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack exactly, because I’m not always sure where that line is, but it feels very sudden and very strong. The second I hear that sharp buzzing by the porch, or if I see one hovering around the flowers, my heart just jumps. It’s like my whole body reacts before I’ve even had time to think.

My hands start shaking, and I get this immediate feeling like, I have to get inside right now. Not in a calm way, like “oh, I should move away,” but more like I can’t stay there. Even if I was just sitting outside or stepping out for a minute, once it’s close to me, I just need to get away from it. So yes, it feels panicky, even if I don’t know if it’s technically a panic attack.
Do you feel this same kind of fear around other insects, or is it only with wasps?

It’s really wasps, mainly. I mean, I don’t love insects in general — I’m not going to say I enjoy things crawling around — but it’s not the same. If I see an ant or a beetle or even a fly, I might be annoyed or want it out of the house, but I don’t get that feeling like something awful is about to happen.

With wasps, it’s completely different. I know, logically, it’s a tiny insect, and I know most people would just swat it away or step aside and not make a big production of it. But for me, if one gets anywhere near me, it feels like real danger, like I have to get away because something terrible is about to happen. It’s not just “oh, that’s unpleasant.” It’s much stronger than that.
